title: fix(fields): take the percent cell's magnitude from the value, not the column name
body:
Fixes #9452

The percent list cell branched on the column's NAME before it looked at the
value: a `/progress|completion/` test against `field.name` decided the column
already held percentage POINTS, so it skipped `percentDisplayValue` — the
declared single source of truth for percent display scaling. A stored `0.5`
rendered `50%` in the record-header summary chip and `1%` in the list cell.

## What changed

`PercentCellRenderer` in `packages/fields/src/index.tsx`:

- `WHOLE_PERCENT_FIELD_PATTERN` and the `isWholePercentField` predicate are gone.
- the number goes through `formatPercent`, which applies `percentDisplayValue`;
- the bar's fill goes through `percentDisplayValue` directly.

No export moved. The renderer's signature is unchanged.

## The second consumer, which the card had not measured

The name predicate had TWO readers and the filing card's value-by-value table
measured only the text. The mini progress bar's fill read the same predicate,
and its non-matching arm was a LOCAL restatement of `percentDisplayValue`'s own
expression rather than a call to it. Measured on the pre-fix tree at
`f0b497921`, through the rendered cell (`en` session, no declared `scale`):

| stored | column name | number (cell text) | bar (`aria-valuenow`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0.5` | `progress` / `completion` / `in_progress_ratio` | `1%` | `0.5` |
| `0.5` | `win_rate` (ordinary percent) | `50%` | `50` |
| `12.3` | every name above | `12%` | `12.3` |
| `57` | every name above | `57%` | `57` |

⭐ So one cell disagreed with ITSELF: a `progress`-named column storing `0.5`
drew a bar 0.5% wide beside the text `1%`. That is a third answer to "is this a
fraction", inside the same renderer, and it is now gone with the other two.

⚠️ One premise correction for the record: the bar's non-matching arm was NOT a
third RULE. Its expression is character-for-character the body of
`percentDisplayValue` — a local COPY, numerically identical, never a divergence.
The hazard was duplication (the drift `percentDisplayValue`'s own doc comment
exists to prevent), not disagreement.

## The measurement that collapsed the fork

The card deliberately left the direction open, so this is a reading and not a
preference. The two paths differ on exactly one input range — a stored value
strictly between `-1` and `1` — so the question is whether anything first-party
puts a sub-1 value in a `progress` / `completion`-named percent column, and
what it means by it.

Reproduce from the repo root — both lines were re-run verbatim in the form
printed here, on this branch:

```bash
# CONTROL — the population. Must be non-zero, or the answer below is a dead grep.
git grep -nE "["']?type["']?[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*["']percent["']" -- . ':!pnpm-lock.yaml' | wc -l

# THE ANSWER — every percent context in the tree whose column name matches the
# pattern that was removed.
git grep -nE "["']?name["']?[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*["'][a-z_]*(progress|completion)[a-z_]*["']" -- . ':!pnpm-lock.yaml' | grep -i percent
```

The control prints **37**. The answer prints **8 lines** — 5 of them this
package's own percent tests, 3 of them first-party field declarations. ⚠️ Read
the second command for what it is: `git grep` prints the PATH with each hit, so
the trailing filter admits a line whose file path says percent as well as one
whose content does; the eight hits were then read individually rather than
counted. Every one of the three declarations is FRACTION-intent:
- `examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas/fields-percent/with-decimal-precision.json`
  declares a `progress` percent field and stores `0.753` in it. That sample is
  published in the docs under "With Precision".
- `packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/InlineFieldInput.test.tsx` pins a
  `completion` percent field storing `0.5`: the editor must show `50`, and
  typing `75` must store `0.75`.
- `examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas/fields-percent/basic-percent-field.json`
  declares a `completion` percent field with no stored value.
- The percent EDIT widget never consulted the name at all. `PercentField` detects
  the whole-percent convention from a declared `max` above `1`. On the two fields
  above — neither declares `max` — the editor read `75.3%` and `50%` while the
  list cell read `1%` and `1%`.
- `content/docs/fields/percent.mdx` states the stored value is "Decimal between 0
  and 1", and its own Use Cases list names "Progress Tracking: Task completion,
  project progress" as percent-field use cases.
- The genuinely whole-percent producers are declared by TYPE, not by name. In the
  sibling platform tree, `task.progress` and `f_progress` are `type: 'progress'`
  with `min: 0` / `max: 100`, and every seeded value is `0` or an integer at or
  above `1` — the range where both rules agree by construction. The only
  `percent`-typed field there that declares `max: 100` is `allocation_percent`,
  whose name the pattern never matched.

⇒ The name test had **no** first-party producer that needed it and **two** that
it misread. That is what collapsed the fork; the direction was not chosen.

⚠️ **The price, stated rather than papered over.** A value strictly between `0`
and `1` stored in a `type: 'progress'` column now reads as a fraction, like
everywhere else. Nothing first-party stores one. A tenant that really did store
sub-1 percentage points in such a column sees those cells move by two orders of
magnitude, and the repair is at the producer. `0` and every value at or above
`1` are byte-identical before and after — that is the card's own `12.3` / `57`
control, kept lit in the pin.

## The unanchored-substring lead

`WHOLE_PERCENT_FIELD_PATTERN` was unanchored and tested against the whole
lowercased name, so it matched on SUBSTRING. Census answer with the control lit
(the same two commands above): no first-party percent column matched by
accident — the three declarations are all deliberate. The one incidental substring
match anywhere is `f_progress` in the platform tree, and it is `type: 'progress'`
already, so the match agreed with its declaration by coincidence rather than by
evidence. The door is shut regardless, because no name reaches the scaling
decision now; `in_progress_ratio` is a pinned row in the new test.

## The pin

`packages/fields/src/__tests__/PercentCellRenderer.nameKeyedScaling-9452.test.tsx`
drives the RENDERED cell — the value text and the `progressbar`'s
`aria-valuenow` — never a local variable and never the formatter in isolation
(a pin on `formatPercent` alone is green on the defect, because the defect was
the renderer choosing not to call it).

- **Pre-fix run, at the branch base `f0b497921`, before any source edit existed:**
  `9 failed | 2 passed (11)`. The failures are the `0.5` rows on all three names,
  on all three assertions (`expected '1%' to contain '50%'`;
  `expected { text: '1%', bar: '0.5' } to deeply equal { text: '50%', bar: '50' }`;
  `expected '0.5' to be '50'`). The 2 passes are the `12.3` and `57` control rows —
  which is what makes the reds a reading rather than a harness that cannot render
  a percent at all.
- **Post-fix:** all 11 green.

## ⚠️ A standing pin was INVERTED, deliberately

`PercentCellRenderer.locale.test.tsx` carried an assertion labelled
must-not-change that read `progress` + `0.5` as `1%`. Read what it was guarding
before treating the inversion as a broken promise: objectui#4553's subject was
the display LOCALE, and that block is its blast-radius guard — it pinned the
magnitudes so a locale change could not move them silently. It was never a
product ruling on which magnitude is right. The guard itself survives intact and
still earns its place; only the magnitude it records has moved, and the reason is
written beside it.

## Premises checked, and the two that were already false

- ✅ Every line number in the dispatch order verified at `f0b497921`: the pattern,
  the renderer, the predicate, the bar arm and the number arm are all exactly
  where the order said.
- ✅ Clause ② re-measured at delivery: `no`. Mechanical floor — added lines
  beginning with `export`: **0**; removed: **0**. The pattern was a bare
  module-private `const` and is now deleted; `PercentCellRenderer` stays exported
  with an unchanged signature (control: 117 lines beginning with `export` in that
  file). No declarable key is added anywhere.
- ⚠️ Falsified: the bar's non-matching arm is a local COPY of
  `percentDisplayValue`, not a third rule — see above.
- ⚠️ Partly falsified: the order's `0.5` reading is right for the number, but the
  bar reported `0.5` where the text said `1%`, so the pre-fix cell was already
  self-inconsistent. That was unmeasured on both the card and the order.
- ✅ Serial constraint confirmed: objectui#8941 touches `packages/fields/package.json`
  only. `origin/main` merged at `f0b497921`, which is this branch's base.

## Verification

| run | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/fields/ packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/InlineFieldInput*.test.tsx` | `167 passed (167)` files, `2903 passed (2903)` tests |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/fields type-check` (`tsc --noEmit` and the test tsconfig) | exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/fields lint` | exit 0, 0 errors |
| `check-control-bytes`, `check-new-cross-file-line-citations`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-pending-changeset-literals`, `check-test-path-roots`, `check-vi-mock-override-shape`, `check-changeset-claims`, `check-unreferenced-sources` | exit 0 each |
| `check-readme-exports` | NOT MEASURED locally — it needs every package's `dist` on disk and says so itself ("run pnpm build first", "the population COLLAPSED"). Not implicated by this diff, which touches no README and no export surface. Declared to CI. |

**Lint scope, declared.** `pnpm lint` here is `turbo run lint`, a per-package
fan-out, and the run above is the COMPLETE unit for the only package this diff
touches. No other unit can move: the flat config extends
`tseslint.configs.recommended`, not the type-checked variant, and declares no
`parserOptions.project` / `projectService`, so type-aware linting is off and a
change inside this package cannot alter a verdict in an untouched file. The rest
of the fan-out, and `pnpm check`, belong to CI.

Verification ran at `git rev-parse --short HEAD` = the tip of this branch.

## Acceptance notes

Siblings noticed and deliberately NOT touched, per the dispatch fences:

- Two comments in `packages/plugin-detail` — in
  `summaryChip.percentConvention-9167.test.tsx` and
  `summaryChip.percentSource-9071.test.tsx` — explain a fixture's name choice by
  saying it avoids "the cell renderer's whole-percent name pattern". That pattern
  no longer exists, so this change makes both sentences stale. Reported rather
  than swept: the order fences the other percent surfaces.
- `PercentFieldMetadata` in `packages/types/src/field-types.ts` declares
  `precision`, `min` and `max` but NOT `scale`, while `PercentCellRenderer` reads
  `field.scale` for its fraction digits. An author reading the declared type
  writes `precision` and silently gets zero decimal places. Adjacent to the
  settled `scale`-vs-`precision` docblock and untouched here.
- `PercentField` (edit) and `PercentCellRenderer` (display) still detect the
  whole-percent convention differently — `max` above 1 versus nothing at all now.
  After this change they agree on every first-party field, but the asymmetry is
  real and is a metadata-surface question, which the order fences off.

Observations only, no card asked for: `formatPercentBody` now has a single
caller; the `Directions` table in `PercentCellRenderer.locale.test.tsx`'s header
is objectui#4553's historical pre-run prediction record and was left as written.
